_meta.generated_for: WP-02 -- making the 14 GlyphMapper methods that accept view= but never use it apply a per-plot `if' qualifier BEFORE the statistic is computed.
_meta.why: These mappers build their own ColumnDataSource from a computed grid, so attaching a CDSView to the returned renderer changes nothing; the INPUT arrays have to be masked.  A test that only checks 'the numbers changed' would pass on a wrong mask, so this fixture records what Stata itself produces for the subset.
_meta.method: Two oracles, recorded side by side wherever both apply.  (1) r()/e() from Stata's own command -- regress, lowess, lpoly, kdensity, fp, and twoway__histogram_gen, the subroutine histogram.ado itself calls.  (2) THE PLOTTED POINTS: each twoway plot is saved to a live-format .gph; `graph use' makes its sersets addressable and `serset set #' + `serset use, clear' loads the exact drawn numbers back into memory.  For mband this reaches the DERIVED serset the graph engine computes at draw time.  Every entry carries the exact Stata command that produced it in its `cmd' / `est_cmd' field.
_meta.precision: Numbers were written with Stata's %20.17g so doubles round-trip.  Values that originate in a serset were stored by the graph engine as FLOATS: compare those to about 1e-6 relative, not exactly.  Values from r()/e() are full double precision.
_meta.how_to_reproduce: arch -arm64 /Applications/StataNow/StataMP.app/Contents/MacOS/stata-mp -b do wp02_truth.do  (NOTE: the bundle also contains a `StataMP' binary which on a case-insensitive filesystem is what `stataMP' resolves to -- that is the GUI binary and it HANGS in -b batch mode.  Use stata-mp.)
_meta.reading_this_fixture: layers.<name>.headline gives the few numbers a test should assert, already split all vs foreign1, with differs_from_unqualified saying whether the qualified answer is actually distinguishable from the full-data one.  The full curves live under layers.<name>.<variant> and under `supporting'.

gaps.what_is_missing: mspline's cross medians are NOT read out of the graph.  Unlike mband, mspline leaves no derived cross-median serset: serset 1 does not exist (rc=111), serset 0 is the raw data and serset 2 is the already-splined curve.
gaps.what_was_done_instead: The cross medians are hand-computed in Stata with Stata's own documented band formula and `collapse (median)', and corroborated against the drawn spline: the spline's x extent equals the first and last hand-computed cross median exactly, on both subsets.
gaps.confidence: high for the x positions and the band count; the interior cross-median Y values are computed, not read from the graph, so treat them as the documented-rule answer rather than as a direct measurement.

gaps.what_is_missing: The rule-of-thumb bandwidth selector itself is not in any .ado -- it lives in compiled Mata -- so this fixture records the bandwidth Stata CHOSE (r(bwidth)) but cannot express it as a formula.
gaps.what_was_done_instead: r(bwidth) is recorded for both subsets: 70.642921355391806 on all 74, 34.904381937757748 on the 22 foreign cars.
gaps.confidence: high for the measured values; no rule is claimed.

gaps.what_is_missing: e(fp_k) does not exist; the selected fractional-polynomial powers are the same (-2, -2) on both subsets, so the POWERS cannot be used to tell a masked fit from an unmasked one.
gaps.what_was_done_instead: The fitted VALUES and the point count are used instead, both of which differ sharply.

gaps.what_is_missing: There is no single kdensity grid: the kdensity COMMAND evaluates over [min-bwidth, max+bwidth] while twoway kdensity evaluates over the plain data range.
gaps.what_was_done_instead: Both grids are recorded in full, under estimation and under plotted_by_twoway, so a test asserts against whichever one dash emulates rather than against a blend of the two.

area.note: area is not a statistic.  What is asserted is the POINT COUNT and the x/y extent of the polygon: with the qualifier applied before the layer is built there must be 22 points spanning weight 1760..3420, not 74 points spanning 1760..4840.

plotted.cmd: twoway area mpg weight if foreign==1

lfit.note: Stata draws the line only over the OBSERVED x range of the estimation sample, so both the coefficients and the endpoints change with the qualifier.

generate double w2 = weight^2 THEN regress mpg weight w2 if foreign==1

plotted.cmd: twoway qfit mpg weight if foreign==1

lfitci.note: Two oracles: the 100-point band twoway actually plotted (serset column order fit, lower, upper, x -- confirmed against the rebuild), and an independent regress + predict xb/stdp rebuild using tcrit = invttail(e(df_r), 0.025).  They agree at both endpoints to float precision.  Note the band's MIN/MAX over the grid is not the endpoint value for the quadratic, which is why the endpoints are listed explicitly.

lowess.note: lowess returns the smooth AT THE OBSERVED x values, one per observation in the estimation sample -- there is no separate grid, so the qualifier changes both the number of smoothed points (74 -> 22) and every value.  bwidth(.8) is Stata's own default, passed explicitly.  The median point is the ceil(n/2)-th observation after sorting on weight, and its x is recorded so the test knows which point it is.

estimation.cmd: lowess mpg weight , bwidth(.8) generate(lw) nograph
lowess mpg weight if foreign==1, bwidth(.8) generate(lw) nograph

plotted.cmd: twoway lowess mpg weight if foreign==1, bwidth(.8)

lpoly.note: lpoly's rule-of-thumb bandwidth is computed from the estimation sample, so it changes with the qualifier (70.64 -> 34.90).  The grid is n() = min(N,50) points across the sample's x range, but grid points with no data inside the kernel window carry a MISSING fit and are not plotted: on the subset 22 of the 50 grid points are missing, so the drawn curve is 28 points and stops at weight 2810.2, well short of the subset maximum of 3420.  The three recorded x points are the first, ceil(n/2)-th and last of the NON-MISSING grid.

estimation.cmd: lpoly mpg weight , degree(0) nograph generate(gx gy)
lpoly mpg weight if foreign==1, degree(0) nograph generate(gx gy)

plotted.cmd: twoway lpoly mpg weight if foreign==1, degree(0)

lpolyci.note: The lpolyci serset does NOT use the (fit, lower, upper, x) column order that lfitci/qfitci/fpfitci use, and r(varnames) comes back empty for a saved .gph, so the four columns were recorded generically and identified afterwards: the column whose range equals the known weight range is x, the column matching the lpoly fit exactly is the fit, and of the remaining two the one with the smaller maximum is lower.  serset_column_roles records the mapping that was derived, and grid_x/fit/lower/upper are kept ROW-ALIGNED on the full 50-point grid (nulls included) so a test can index by grid position.  WATCH OUT: with degree(0) and this bandwidth many grid points hold too little data for a band -- on the 22-car subset only 23 of the 50 grid points have a CI at all and only 15 of those are wider than 1e-4, and BOTH endpoints are degenerate (lower == upper == fit).  On the full 74 cars the corresponding counts are 45 and 41, and only the last endpoint is degenerate.  Assert on widest_band_point and on the counts, not on the endpoints.

foreign1.cmd: twoway lpolyci mpg weight if foreign==1, degree(0)

fpfit.note: twoway fpfit evaluates at the DISTINCT OBSERVED x values of the estimation sample, sorted -- not on a fixed grid.  n_points therefore equals n_distinct_weight for that subset (64 for all, 22 for foreign==1), which is itself a strong assertion that the qualifier reached the input arrays.  e(fp_powers) is the CANDIDATE power set; e(fp_fp) is what fp actually selected (here (-2,-2) both ways, so the powers are NOT what distinguishes the two fits -- the fitted values are).

estimation.est_cmd: fp <weight>, replace: regress mpg <weight> if foreign==1

plotted.cmd: twoway fpfit mpg weight if foreign==1
twoway fpfitci mpg weight if foreign==1

histogram.note: The default and the explicit-density runs are byte-identical, which is how this fixture establishes that DENSITY is Stata's default bar height; the frequency run is recorded beside them so a test can tell the two apart.  The bin count follows max(1, int(min(sqrt(N), 10*ln(N)/ln(10)))) on the SUBSET's N: 8 bins over [12,41] for all 74 cars, 4 bins over [14,41] for the 22 foreign ones.  map_histogram reaches its input through the module-level _extract_finite(source, yvar) at line 4713; that helper's other two callers (7778 and 7856, the slider and range filter builders) must keep seeing the UNFILTERED column.

kdensity.note: The bandwidth Stata chose is 1.9746142000627720 on all 74 and 2.5167731010341630 on the 22 foreign cars, and both reproduce the documented rule 0.9*min(sd,(p75-p25)/1.349)/N^0.2 exactly, so a test can assert either the number or the rule.  NOTE the two evaluation grids differ and both are recorded: the kdensity COMMAND evaluates over [min-bw, max+bw], while twoway kdensity evaluates over the plain data range [min, max].  map_kdensity reaches its input through _extract_finite(source, yvar) at line 4877 -- same shared-helper caution as map_histogram.

kdensity mpg if foreign==1, n(10) nograph generate(kx kd)

plotted_by_twoway.cmd: twoway kdensity mpg if foreign==1, n(10)

mband.note: Read from the DERIVED serset (set 1) that the graph engine computes at draw time, so these are the cross medians actually drawn.  The band count Stata used is 9 on all 74 and 5 on the 22 foreign cars.  That matches round(min(sqrt(N), 10*log10(N))) -- the rule measured across 14 (N,bands) pairs in stat_truth.json -- and NOT the documented max(10, round(10*log10(N))), which would give 19 and 13.  supporting.mband_cross_medians_by_band_count holds the hand-computed medians for every band count 2..30 on both subsets, so an implementation that picks a different band count can still be checked against the right column.

plotted_cross_medians.cmd: twoway mband mpg weight if foreign==1

mspline.note: mspline has no derived cross-median serset to read (set 1 does not exist; rc=111).  What CAN be read is set 2, the spline curve the engine drew, and its x extent pins the cross medians exactly: 1980..4780 for all 74 and 1990..3295 for the 22 foreign cars, which are precisely the first and last hand-computed cross medians at the documented band count (9 and 5).  The cross medians themselves are therefore HAND-COMPUTED with Stata's own documented formula max(min(round(10*log10(N)), round(sqrt(N))), min(2,N)) and collapse (median), and the spline curve is recorded beside them as the corroborating measurement rather than as the primary assertion.  In this dataset the mspline and mband band counts coincide (9 and 5) and the cross medians are identical, which the fixture lets you verify by comparing the two layers.

cross_medians.cmd: sysuse auto -- keep (all) -- generate band = min(max(floor((weight-min)/((max-min)/B))+1,1),B) -- collapse (median) weight mpg, by(band)
sysuse auto -- keep if foreign==1 -- generate band = min(max(floor((weight-min)/((max-min)/B))+1,1),B) -- collapse (median) weight mpg, by(band)
